newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: London robustas seen up on meteoric New York rally.
newsitem.headline: London robustas seen up on meteoric New York rally.

text.p: Far East coffee dealers said London robusta futures will probably jump by between US$50-$150 later on Thursday as they chase a galloping rally in New York.

"The way New York is performing, I would say London will be $100-$150 up. But I don't think they'll make it. Sixty sounds more like it," a coffee dealer for a commodity firm in Singapore said. "We're seeing fantastic levels the past two days."
"London is not as emotional as New York. It should be up another $50-$60," a European coffee dealer added.
One dealer said LIFFE's July robusta contract should easily pierce $2,300 and "the near-term resistance will be $2,500."
London's July robusta contract shot up on Wednesday to end at $2,260 a tonne, a huge $158 up on the day and just off its intra-day peak of $2,262.

The market was inspired by a blistering rally in New York, where the July arabica contract hit a new life-of-contract high of 297.00 U.S. cents a lb before finishing 21.25 cents up on the day at 295.55 cents.
One dealer predicted robusta prices still have a lot of room on the upside.
"There'll come a time when arabica become too expensive. Then they'll switch to robustas and you may see a further price spike," he said.
The surging prices triggered jitters among some Asian coffee dealers that a few exporters in Indonesia may opt to default on their deliveries.
"I'm sure they're thinking of default, especially those selling arabica beans. Some of them are hurting, especially those guys who pre-sold their crop earlier this month," one dealer said.

Indonesia's key Grade 40 coffee, 80 defects, was quoted by the trade on Thursday at $2,000/010 a tonne FOB Lampung, up almost a third from the figure at the end of April of $1,350/400 a tonne on the same basis.
"People in Indonesia who are just beginning to sell their crop are very comfortable with these prices," a dealer said. "The producers are pretty happy at what they're seeing."
Exporters in Vietnam, which the trade believes may still have about 25,000 tonnes of robusta beans, are holding back on their sales on the the belief that prices will move higher.
Vietnam's benchmark Grade 2 coffee, 8.0 percent black and broken, was seen by the trade at $1,960/970 a tonne FOB Saigon against a quote on April 30 of $1,300/400 a tonne FOB Saigon.
